title: Fourteen Autumns and One Short List
subtitle: 选举制度 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 选举制度（人与社会·历史社会与文化）
meta: 主题语境：选举制度（人与社会·历史社会与文化）　|　核心词汇：election　|　正文 342 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 election 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1950 my father ① watched an election that no neighbour in the town would have described, and he said the watching was the whole of the autumn. The ② election, meaning the vote and not the winning, ran fourteen autumns and stayed unnamed in the book; an election, he said, is the only thing in a town that is judged by how long it is left undescribed.

Every ③ election in that town had the same short list at the end of it, and the ④ election at the end, meaning the one they kept for the parish and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. An election, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to describe; my father said the describing is the part that fills fourteen autumns.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the election was the whole of the story, meaning the winning and not the vote. The ⑥ election, meaning the winning and not any of that, is the only thing in a story that everybody hopes for and nobody mentions; election, he said, is either something you watch or the only word that means both a vote and a winning. He said the winning is the part they remember.

By 1959 the ⑦ election had become a line in a notice, and the notice had become an argument about the short list. The ⑧ election of the whole thing, my father wrote in October, was one town and fourteen autumns of describing; election, he said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to describe. She said the describing was never mentioned.

The ⑨ election I remember is the one named in the notice, which passed in 1971 and is still described as the quietest in the town. An ⑩ election, my mother said in 1973, is the only one that improves by being described; every election, she said, is a winning that has agreed to look like a vote. She said the winning was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 选举（指那个镇子上经历过的那一次）
B. n. 选举（指那次选举本身，与当选相对）
C. 固定搭配：watch an election 观看一次选举
D. n. 选举（指留给教区的那一次）
E. n. 选举（抽象总称，指一个镇子的选举之事）
F. n. 选举（指公告上写到、被列名的那一次）
G. n. 当选；当选的机会（指故事里人人都盼却无人提及的那样东西）
H. n. 当选（抽象总称，指人人都盼却无人提及的那种结果）

items.q: watched an election that no neighbour in the town would have described
The election, meaning the vote and not the winning
the election was the whole of the story
the election had become a line in a notice
The election of the whole thing
An election, my mother said in 1973

answers.why: watch an election 意为“观看一次选举”，1950 年父亲观看了一场镇子上没有一位邻居肯描述出来的选举。
election 意为“选举”，指那次选举本身而不是当选，它经过了十四个秋天而在簿子上没有名字。
election 意为“选举”，指那个镇子上的每一次选举，每一次后头都有同一张短短的名单。
election 意为“选举”，指留给教区的那一次，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
election 意为“当选、当选的机会”，指故事里人人都盼却无人提及的那样东西，叔叔说这次当选就是那个故事的全部。
election 意为“当选”，指人人都盼却无人提及的那种结果而不是那次选举，是故事里人人都盼、却无人提及的东西。
election 意为“选举”，指公告上写到、被列名的那一次，到 1959 年这次选举成了公告里的一行。
election 意为“选举”，父亲十月写道，整件事的选举之事是一个镇子和十四个秋天的讲述。
election 意为“选举”，我记得的是公告上列名的那一次，1971 年过去了，至今仍被说成镇子上最安静的一次。
election 为抽象总称，母亲 1973 年说，一次选举是唯一会因为被好好讲述而变得更好的东西。

那次选举，指的是那次选举本身而不是当选，经过了十四个秋天而在簿子上没有名字。（election）
那个镇子上每一次选举后头都有同一张短短的名单。（election）
末尾那一次选举，指的是他们留给教区的那一次，是唯一有人谢过两次的。（election）
叔叔说这次当选就是那个故事的全部，指的是当选而不是那次选举。（election）
